objections.claim: The anchor is not a unique section identifier: heading slugs can repeat within a spec, so the design binds objections to a name that can occur multiple times, not to the specific section attacked.
objections.evidence: Spec §3 definition; §4 Edge cases (duplicate slugs are the consumer's concern).
objections.predicted_consequence: With two same-slug sections, every anchored objection binds to all matches and FAFF-930's Argument-B lookup can attach the wrong defence, defeating the binding goal.

objections.claim: The producer/consumer slug agreement depends on an unestablished input invariant: nothing establishes the refuter receives the same raw source text the assembler indexes.
objections.evidence: Spec §4 (same source line by construction; assembler indexes the same raw source lines) vs the refuter prompt (spec supplied as the diff); FAFF-930 unbuilt.
objections.predicted_consequence: If the refuter sees rendered or normalized text rather than the raw markdown, emitted anchors systematically mismatch the consumer's index, degrading silently to orchestrator:undefended.

objections.claim: The slug rule creates a second dialect beside the existing capped convention; future authors may confuse or reuse the wrong one.
objections.predicted_consequence: A long heading capped in ADR/decision/PRD contexts produces a different anchor here, increasing cross-artifact mismatch or accidental reuse of the capped rule.

objections.claim: The prose-identity oracle covers the rule sentence and slug strings but not the omit rule: a prompt that drops the omit instruction passes every named gate, and the producer emits a sentinel or fabricated slug instead of omitting.
objections.evidence: DONE producer item (omit rule a separate clause with no mechanical assertion).
objections.predicted_consequence: A non-empty spec_anchor that matches no heading rides the round record as a misleading value; absence-is-the-signal is violated at the producer end and no named test catches it.

objections.claim: The byte-identical churn/convergence assertion names no fixture pair or diff procedure; it is a property, not a test.
objections.evidence: Scenario 2 and the carry-through DONE item.
objections.predicted_consequence: A serialization/field-order change invisible to existing tests could break a byte-comparing downstream consumer; discovered only when FAFF-930 lands.
